Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier today — the team at VantageCare is excited about Redwood Dedicated for inference and the VPC/private control plane option given our PHI requirements. A couple of procurement asks came up after the demo:

- Can you confirm whether onboarding credits / pilot subsidy can be applied against the first two months of usage for a dedicated pool?
- We need a one-off rate alignment for the first 6 months (we expect uneven ramp) — specifically a temporary 25% off list on the Dedicated unit rates with a hard cap on total subsidy.

I attached the SOW draft and redlined the bit about logs (VantageCare_SOW_v2.pdf). Procurement asked if Redwood would sign off on a limited onboarding subsidy and a capped credit that can be invoiced as a contra-charge rather than a line-item discount.

Can you advise next steps and whether this needs executive signoff? We are trying to close by next-week EOD.

On Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 10:03 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding VantageCare procurement request. Key asks: a) two-month onboarding subsidy (applied as credit) b) temporary 25% off Dedicated unit rate for first 6 months with an overall cap c) SOW updates + DocuSign.

Quick recommendation from Commercial Ops:

1) Approve a one-time onboarding subsidy applied as a contra-credit to the first invoice(s) up to a $75k gross cap. This preserves list pricing downstream and is consistent with precedent for similar mid-market healthcare pilots.

2) Instead of a 25% headline off list, propose a blended temporary rate with a floor guarantee:
   - Months 1–2: onboarding subsidy applied as credit (no permanent list change)
   - Months 3–6: 15% temporary rate reduction on Dedicated unit rates, automatically reverting to list thereafter
   - Subsidy + temporary rate reductions together cannot exceed $120k total (the cap)

3) Require a 6-month usage report and executive review clause — if usage is >1.5x forecast we convert to committed tier pricing with retrospective true-up.

4) Commercial language: we can accept the credit vs discount structuring but need the contra-credit to be reflected in our invoicing (memo field) and a short SOW amendment. Finance to approve final wording to avoid revenue recognition complications.

If Finance (Markus) confirms the $120k cap and the contra-credit approach is acceptable, we can send a short approval memo to Aisha and proceed with an amended SOW + DocuSign this week.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Cc: aisha.patel@vantagecare.com
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Next steps on Dedicated + private deployment pricing

Thanks for the clear framing — I reviewed the numbers and precedent. Finance signoff (CFO) for a bounded subsidy is acceptable under the following conditions:

- Approve the contra-credit structure with a gross cap of $120,000 (agrees with Marissa).
- Credits must be amortized and the SOW must include an explicit cap and expiry date (6 months).
- The subsidy cannot reduce billable minimums for Dedicated pool commitments; it must be a contra credit on initial invoices only.
- Require a one-time internal signoff matrix: Sales Lead (Karthik), Commercial Ops (Marissa), and CFO (Markus) must initial the approval memo.

Please incorporate the above into an approval memo that Tessa can send to Aisha; include the cap, contra-credit mechanics, audit clause, and a requirement to convert to committed pricing or true-up if usage exceeds forecasts. Legal should do a brief SOW amendment (no more than 2 bullets) and we route to DocuSign.

If you want I can sign the memo today — confirm and I’ll reply-all with the executive signoff.

-Markus
